systems.kitPhilosophy: The drum ships full of the "smart, hard-to-find, corrosion-critical" bits — all 316 rigging (cable, thimbles, clips, turnbuckles, pad-eyes), the bolt/isolation kit, cosmetic caps, foam kit, mast base and battery box — everything under 33 in that a hardware store won't reliably stock in marine grade. The three long rigid members that physically can't fit the 22.5x33 in drum (dock floats/hull pipe, aluminum frame stock, mast tube) are a printed cut-list the builder buys locally, because shipping 10 ft stock costs more than the metal.

parts.name: Pontoons / hulls (Route A: foam-cored HDPE dock floats)
parts.chosenComponent: BARR Plastics PermaFloat rotomolded HDPE + EPS-foam-core dock float, ~24x48x16 in class (size to >=2x payload; ~590-900 lb buoyancy each, molded bolt flanges)
parts.vendor: BARR Plastics / Dock Builders Supply (Permafloat) / Great Northern Docks
parts.qty: 2 (add a 3rd if drum runs fuller than ~40 gal)
parts.fitsNote: A 24x48x16 in float dwarfs the 22.5 in drum bore in every axis — cannot ship inside. Bulky/light, cheapest freight is local pickup or the dock-supplier's own LTL.
parts.upgrade: Two full 55-gal HDPE drums as pontoons (near-free if salvaged) undersize the payload; better upgrade is upsizing to a 24x72 in PermaFloat pair (~1,200+ lb pair) so the drum can run full without a 3rd float.

parts.name: Pontoons / hulls (Route B: round-tube look)
parts.chosenComponent: 12 in HDPE / DR17 poly pipe, 10 ft, filled SOLID with 2-lb foam; or Charlotte 6 in PVC (classic look, but undersized — see note)
parts.vendor: Local plastics/irrigation yard (HDPE) or Home Depot (PVC)
parts.fitsNote: 10 ft pipe is ~3.6x the drum's 33 in interior length — impossible to ship in-drum; the rule sends any >33 in rigid member local.
parts.upgrade: Route A dock floats are strictly better (unsinkable, UV-stable, no glued seam to flood the hollow tube); keep Route B only for the original tube aesthetic and then fill solid, not partial.

parts.name: Deck frame — aluminum ladder (Route A, recommended)
parts.chosenComponent: 6061-T6 aluminum square tube, 2x2 in x 0.125 in wall (bolted ladder: 2 cross-beams + perimeter + center bay)
parts.qty: ~40-60 ft (measure to your beam & hull length)
parts.fitsNote: Sold in 8-24 ft sticks; even a 4 ft cut exceeds the 33 in drum length. Local pickup avoids per-stick oversize freight that can exceed the metal cost.
parts.upgrade: 6061-T6 is the right call over PVC (no creep, ratable, bolts together). If budget allows, 2x3 in x 0.125 in for the two spanwise cross-beams stiffens the drum bay for little added weight.

parts.name: Frame joint hardware (bolted gussets / angle brackets)
parts.chosenComponent: 6061 aluminum angle + flat-bar gussets, drilled for 5/16 or 3/8 in bolts at every joint (fabbed from offcuts)
parts.fitsNote: Short angle/gusset offcuts (<12 in) ship flat in the drum; if cut from the same local stock, buy with the frame.
parts.upgrade: Bolted aluminum gussets replace the as-built's unrated furniture-grade PVC 4-way fittings entirely — the single biggest structural fix. No plastic fitting belongs in the load path.

parts.name: Mast
parts.chosenComponent: 6061-T6 aluminum tube, 2 in OD, ~6 ft, set in a bolted base flange
parts.fitsNote: ~6 ft length is ~2x the 33 in drum interior — ships local with the frame stock.
parts.upgrade: On Route A the mast is structural-only (carries panel/turbine); a low-mounted battery does the stability work, so no need to oversize the mast for tensegrity preload.

parts.name: Mast base flange / socket
parts.chosenComponent: 2 in bolt-down aluminum floor flange / weld-on base socket
parts.fitsNote: Palm-sized flange packs flat in the drum.
parts.upgrade: On Route B add a threaded jack-screw adjuster at the base to set tensegrity preload to torque; unnecessary on the bolted Route A frame.
parts.link: search: 2 inch aluminum bolt down floor flange

parts.name: Rigging cable (Route B tensegrity)
parts.chosenComponent: 1/8 in 7x19 Type 316 stainless aircraft cable
parts.fitsNote: Coils to a ~10 in loop — ships easily in the drum. This is exactly the corrosion-critical part a builder should NOT substitute with hardware-store galvanized.
parts.upgrade: Deleted entirely on the bolted aluminum Route A. If keeping tensegrity, 316 (not 304) is the pond-water-correct grade.

parts.name: Wire-rope thimbles (Route B)
parts.chosenComponent: 1/8 in Type 316 stainless wire-rope thimbles
parts.fitsNote: Coin-sized; ships loose in a hardware bag inside the drum.
parts.upgrade: Swageless mechanical terminals (Hayn Hi-Mod / Suncor) eliminate thimbles AND clips for full-strength, tool-free eyes — pricier but foolproof for a DIY builder.

parts.name: Wire-rope clips (saddle clamps, Route B)
parts.chosenComponent: 1/8 in Type 316 stainless U-bolt wire-rope clips (DuraBrite / US Stainless)
parts.fitsNote: Small; ships in the fastener bag. Include a printed 'never saddle a dead horse' + 4.5 ft-lb torque card.
parts.upgrade: Same swageless-terminal upgrade as thimbles retires clips entirely and removes the #1 rigging error (saddle on the dead end).

parts.name: Turnbuckles (Route B upper-half tensioners)
parts.chosenComponent: 316 stainless 3/8 in x 6 in hook-and-eye turnbuckle
parts.vendor: e-Rigging / US Rigging / Stainless Steel Marine
parts.fitsNote: ~6 in closed — well under drum length, ships inside.
parts.upgrade: Deleted on Route A. If kept, jaw-and-jaw (vs hook) turnbuckles won't unhook under a slack cycle — safer on a moving raft than open hooks.

parts.name: Pad-eyes / lifting eyes
parts.chosenComponent: 316 stainless heavy-duty diamond/cast pad eye (~2000 lb WLL, 1/4 in fasteners)
parts.qty: 4 corner lift points (+4-8 more for Route B cable anchors)
parts.fitsNote: Fist-sized castings; ship in-drum. Label the 4 corner ones 'LIFT ONLY HERE.'
parts.upgrade: For the four hoist points, a forged (not cast) 316 pad eye or a bolt-through backing-plate eye gives a higher, more trustworthy WLL than economy cast eyes.

parts.name: 316 bolt / nut / washer + galvanic-isolation kit
parts.chosenComponent: 316 SS hex-cap-screw assortment (e.g. BoltsandNuts 574-pc) + nylon shoulder isolation washers + nylon flat washers + anti-seize
parts.vendor: BoltsandNuts.com / Marine Bolt Supply / McMaster (nylon shoulder washers) + Amazon (anti-seize)
parts.fitsNote: Compact kit box + washer packs ship in-drum. Nylon shoulder washers at every Al-to-316 interface are the corrosion firewall a builder rarely sources on their own.
parts.upgrade: Add a small tube of Tef-Gel (marine dielectric) instead of generic anti-seize at the aluminum/stainless joints — it's the boatyard standard for stopping galvanic seizing on fasteners.

parts.name: Flotation pour foam (Route B pipe hulls only)
parts.chosenComponent: 2-part 2-lb-density closed-cell polyurethane pour foam, 2-gal kit (TotalBoat / True Composites)
parts.qty: ~2 gal per hull (fill SOLID in ~5 staged lifts)
parts.fitsNote: Two 1-gal jugs stand upright in the 33 in drum. DELETED on Route A (dock floats are already foam-cored).
parts.upgrade: None needed — 2-lb closed-cell is the correct marine grade; just pour SOLID (not the as-built's partial pour that left the tube mostly hollow).

parts.name: Cosmetic nose caps + googly eyes (the manatee face)
parts.chosenComponent: 6 in Sch-40 domed PVC slip cap (DURA 447-060) + large adhesive googly eyes
parts.vendor: Home Depot / PVC Fittings Online + Amazon (googly eyes)
parts.fitsNote: 6 in caps nest inside the 22.5 in bore. Eyes go on the two FORWARD caps only — never the reactor drum (grounding note is emphatic).
parts.upgrade: Foam nose cones (shaped, lighter) read more 'manatee' than flat-domed caps and add a touch of reserve buoyancy at the bow; purely cosmetic either way.

parts.name: Vented battery box (mounts battery low as ballast)
parts.chosenComponent: Attwood Power Guard Group 27 vented marine battery box + hold-down strap (350 lb strap)
parts.fitsNote: ~13x8x10 in box fits inside the 22.5 in bore. Mounting it low/central is the free capsize fix.
parts.upgrade: If going LiFePO4, a low-profile group-24 box lowers CG further; the vent matters only for flooded/AGM, so a sealed LiFePO4 can sit in a simpler strapped tray even lower.

parts.name: Drum cradle straps
parts.chosenComponent: 2 in x 10-12 ft heavy-duty ratchet straps (2-pack) over a bolted aluminum center-bay saddle
parts.fitsNote: Straps coil flat in the drum; the saddle itself is cut from the local aluminum frame stock.
parts.upgrade: Swap ratchet straps for cam-buckle stainless-hardware straps (won't rust-seize) or a molded 55-gal drum saddle; the ~460 lb full drum is the heaviest single mass and must not shift underway.

systems.kitPhilosophy: Almost the entire power subsystem is small, rugged, and drum-packable, so the "brains + protection + metering" all SHIP IN THE DRUM as a sealed electronics bundle (MPPT, shunt, fusing, distribution, relays, enclosure, control boards, wiring kit). The two heavy commodity items — the 12V battery (lithium ground-ship/hazmat rules, and it's a swap-anywhere part) and the rigid solar panel (fragile glass, and locally-stocked) — are SOURCE-LOCALLY on a cut-list. The control brain is presented as three honest tiers, not one pick: (A) no dedicated brain — the Victron MPPT's own programmable load output + low-voltage-disconnect runs the pump on a timer (baseline, recommended); (B) a ~$20 analog BEAM phototrope kit if light-seeking steering thrusters are fitted; (C) a ~$10 ESP32 if the builder wants programmable duty-cycling, Wi-Fi/BLE telemetry, and data logging. No machine learning anywhere — this is cheap, proven, un-exotic hardware, and that is the point.

parts.name: Solar panel (primary + only baseline generation)
parts.chosenComponent: Renogy 50W 12V Monocrystalline Compact (RNG-50D-SS), ~20 x 26.8 x 1.2 in, ~8 lb
parts.fitsNote: The compact rigid 50W (~20x27in) actually fits inside the 22.5x33in drum on the diagonal, but it is fragile glass — better boxed separately or sourced locally. Manual specs 45W; a 50W compact is the closest current stock item and gives ~120-170 Wh/day after derating.
parts.upgrade: Step to a 100W panel (Renogy RNG-100D, ~$95) IF the payload/float budget allows the extra weight — doubles daily harvest and lets the cavitation batch run longer; pair with a 75/15 or 100/20 MPPT. Or a semi-flexible 50-100W panel (Renogy flexible, ~$80-140) to stow flat and shed the glass fragility.

parts.name: MPPT solar charge controller (regulation + duty-cycle timer + LVD)
parts.chosenComponent: Victron SmartSolar MPPT 75/15 (SCC075015060), Bluetooth
parts.fitsNote: Palm-sized (~5x4x2in). Ships in the drum. This is the keystone electronics upgrade: +15-30% harvest vs PWM, built-in reverse-polarity protection (deletes the old 50A blocking diode), and a programmable load output + low-voltage-disconnect that replaces the hand-soldered trim-pot perfboard as the pump duty-cycle timer.
parts.upgrade: For a 45-50W panel only, the 75/10 (~$85) is technically enough (panel Isc ~3A << 10A) and saves ~$25. Go UP to 100/20 (~$150) only if upsizing to a 100W+ panel. The 75/15 is the sweet spot — headroom for a 100W panel without overpaying.

parts.name: Battery monitor / coulomb-counting shunt (the missing power-budget instrument)
parts.chosenComponent: Victron SmartShunt 500A/50mV IP65, Bluetooth (SHU050150050)
parts.vendor: Amazon / Off Grid Stores / Battle Born
parts.fitsNote: Small (~4x3x2in). Ships in drum. Installed in the battery NEGATIVE path so all current passes through it — this single part retires the venture's biggest open question (does Wh-in vs oil-out close?) by logging it automatically every run. Pairs with the MPPT's harvest log over the same VictronConnect app.
parts.upgrade: Two ways: DOWN to a bare INA226 breakout (~$15) if the builder is comfortable with an Arduino/ESP32 reading it (loses the polished app, keeps the physics); or the SmartShunt 300A (~$100) is more than enough for this <10A load and saves a few dollars. The 500A is only 'bigger' — not better here.

parts.name: 12V battery (overnight store + low-mounted stability ballast)
parts.chosenComponent: LiTime 12V 50Ah LiFePO4, built-in 50A BMS, ~11.6 lb (or Ampere Time 12V 50Ah equivalent)
parts.fitsNote: Dimensionally it WOULD fit the drum (~7.7x6.6x6.8in), but lithium cells carry ground-ship/hazmat restrictions and it is a swap-anywhere commodity — cheaper and simpler for the builder to buy locally. Mount it LOW and central between the hulls: the manual makes it double as capsize ballast, the cheapest stability fix in the build.
parts.upgrade: Step to 12V 100Ah LiFePO4 (~$200-240) for genuine ~2-day autonomy margin and more ballast mass — highly worth it since the whole rig runs as a solar-charged batch process and reserve energy sets the duty cycle. Or a Bluetooth-BMS version (LiTime 50Ah TM, ~$180) to see state-of-charge on the phone. AGM (Group 24, ~$130) is the cheap heavy fallback but has worse cycle life with no LVD headroom.

parts.name: Main terminal fuse (life-safety — was completely absent on the built rig)
parts.chosenComponent: Blue Sea 5178 MRBF 60A terminal fuse + Blue Sea 5191 MRBF terminal fuse block/holder
parts.fitsNote: Tiny; ships in drum. Bolts directly to the battery positive post BEFORE any wire leaves it. A 12V LiFePO4/AGM bus can source hundreds of amps into a fault — this is the single cheapest fire-safety part in the whole machine and it was missing entirely. Do not energize without it.
parts.upgrade: Size to ACTUAL peak load, not habit: for the baseline diaphragm-pump rig, a 30A MRBF (Blue Sea 5177, ~$12) is correct and safer (trips sooner). Reserve 60A+ only if a 1/2-hp motor pump is fitted. Right-sizing the fuse IS the upgrade.

parts.name: Fused distribution block (per-branch protection + negative bus)
parts.chosenComponent: Blue Sea 5025 ST-Blade 6-circuit fuse block with negative bus and cover
parts.vendor: Off Grid Stores / West Marine / Amazon
parts.fitsNote: ~5x3x2in; ships in drum. Combined switched-positive fused bus + a negative bus bar in one part (single-point ground, no ground loops). Every load branch — pump, each annunciator, controller — gets its own ATO/ATC fuse sized to the LOAD.
parts.upgrade: 12-circuit version (Blue Sea 5026, ~$60) if adding thrusters, ESP32, lights, and horns crowds 6 circuits. For a truly minimal baseline, an inline ATC fuse holder per branch (~$2 ea) is cheaper but messier — the block is worth it for serviceability.

parts.name: Load switching relays (replace the hot, lossy Fotek DC SSRs)
parts.chosenComponent: OLS / True Mods 12V 40A waterproof 5-pin SPDT Bosch-style relay w/ sealed socket & harness
parts.fitsNote: Sealed, cheap, marine-rated; ship in drum. Each old Fotek SSR-40 DD burned ~5W as heat while conducting — four of them could quietly eat a third of a 45W budget. Sealed relays have near-zero drop, need no heatsink, and are not polarity-sensitive.
parts.upgrade: Logic-level MOSFET module (IRF3205 / IRLB8721 high-side switch board, ~$8) — silent, zero mechanical wear, and can PWM the pump for speed/duty control off the ESP32. The relay is the rugged simple default; the MOSFET is the smarter path if a microcontroller is aboard.

parts.name: Schottky flyback diodes (across each inductive load)
parts.chosenComponent: 1N5822 3A 40V Schottky (assorted 10-pack)
parts.fitsNote: Loose components; ship in drum. One across each inductive load (pump motor, each air horn) to clamp switch-off kickback and protect the relay/MOSFET.
parts.upgrade: None needed — a 1N5822 is correct and pennies. If MOSFET modules with integrated flyback are used, these become spares.

parts.name: IP66 enclosure + cable glands + breather vent (waterproofing package)
parts.chosenComponent: Polycarbonate IP66/IP67 hinged junction box ~8x6x4in (Zulkit/Polycase) + PG/NPT nylon cable gland assortment + Blue Sea 1000-class / Gore vent plug
parts.fitsNote: Ships in drum (and can nest the small electronics inside it for packing). Box mounts above the splash line; glands go LOW on a side wall, the breather vent HIGH; drip loops on every entry. Water ingress is the #1 failure mode of a floating electronics box — the built rig had a bare perfboard in an open box.
parts.upgrade: For genuine salt exposure, a marine box with 316 stainless glands (Index Marine WB61, ~$40-60) resists pitting — overkill for a freshwater pond but the right call near brackish water. Add a silica-gel desiccant pack (~$5) inside either box.

parts.name: Conformal coating (seal all PCBs against condensation)
parts.chosenComponent: MG Chemicals 422B Silicone Modified Conformal Coating (aerosol)
parts.fitsNote: One aerosol can; ships in drum (check carrier aerosol rules). Coat the MPPT-adjacent boards, relay/MOSFET modules, control board, and voltmeter — belt-and-suspenders with the IP66 box against the humid, splashy environment.
parts.upgrade: MG Chemicals 419D acrylic (~$16) is easier to rework/solder-through if the builder expects to revise the boards; 422B is more moisture-durable for a set-and-forget build.

parts.name: Control brain — OPTION B: BEAM analog phototrope kit (only if steering thrusters fitted)
parts.chosenComponent: Discrete kit: 74HC14 + 74HC125 logic, PN2222A/PN2907A + 2N3904/2N3906 H-bridge transistors, 1N4148 flyback diodes, 2x photodiodes, R/C timing set (0.1uF, 3M/10M)
parts.fitsNote: A handful of chips and passives; ships in drum. Public-domain BEAM/Braitenberg topology — two photodiodes bias an analog 'Nv neuron' oscillator that pulses H-bridges to steer the raft toward the brightest water (a proxy for a surface bloom). No processor, no code, no 'AI'. Bench-verify on a scope that the microcore oscillates before water.
parts.upgrade: Skip the discrete build entirely and do steering in software on the ESP32 (Option C) reading the same two photodiodes — far easier to tune, and you get telemetry for free. The analog board is the honest 'no-firmware' path; the ESP32 is the practical one.

parts.name: Control brain — OPTION C: ESP32 (programmable duty-cycle + BLE/Wi-Fi telemetry + logging)
parts.chosenComponent: ESP32-WROOM-32 DevKit v1 (dual-core, Wi-Fi + BLE)
parts.fitsNote: Thumb-sized; ships in drum. Replaces the obsolete/discontinued MIT Super Cricket and the false ~1m IrDA 'telemetry' claim with real Wi-Fi/BLE. Can run the pump duty cycle, read the shunt (INA226) and photodiodes, drive MOSFET switches, and log every run — genuine telemetry for ~$10.
parts.upgrade: LilyGo T-Display / Heltec ESP32 with onboard OLED + LiPo (~$15-22) adds a field debug screen and a backup rail — handy for on-dock diagnostics without a laptop.

parts.name: LCD glance voltmeter (kept as at-a-glance bus display)
parts.chosenComponent: 0.28in / 0.36in DC digital voltmeter module (or 16x2 LCD DC volt module)
parts.fitsNote: Tiny; ships in drum. Carried over from the original as a dumb glance display across the bus. It shows voltage only — the SmartShunt is what actually captures current/Wh, which is the number that matters.
parts.upgrade: Largely redundant once the SmartShunt's Bluetooth app is in hand — keep it only if the builder wants a no-phone glance readout. A combo volt+amp panel meter (~$12) is a marginally better dumb display.

parts.name: Wiring, terminals & interconnect kit
parts.chosenComponent: Marine-grade tinned duplex/primary wire (10/12/14 AWG), adhesive-lined heat-shrink ring/spade terminals, heat-shrink tubing, cable ties
parts.fitsNote: Short spools, connectors, and heat-shrink SHIP IN DRUM as a kit; long homerun runs are trivially SOURCED LOCALLY once the built layout is measured (run lengths are UNKNOWN until the frame exists). Tinned copper resists corrosion; crimp adhesive-lined terminals and add drip loops.
parts.upgrade: A pre-assembled marine wiring kit (Ancor/heat-shrink-terminal assortment, ~$50) saves sourcing time; step battery-to-MPPT/main-fuse leads up to 8-10 AWG tinned for the higher-current legs if a bigger pump is fitted.

parts.name: OPTIONAL: balanced ultracap surge module (only if a high-inrush 1/2-hp motor pump is fitted)
parts.chosenComponent: Eaton XLM/XLR 16V balanced supercapacitor module + current-limiting pre-charge resistor
parts.fitsNote: DELETED on the baseline — the battery buffers the small diaphragm pump. Ships in drum only if the builder chooses a high-inrush motor pump. MUST be pre-charged through a resistor: a discharged 2200F-class cap is a dead short that will arc-weld terminals. This replaces the original's undocumented, unbalanced 2200F canister + contradictory 3F cap.
parts.upgrade: None on baseline (the correct move is to NOT fit it). If a big pump forces the issue, a factory-balanced module with built-in cell balancing is the only safe choice over loose series cells.

systems.kitPhilosophy: The 55-gal drum is the reactor, the separator, AND the outer shipping crate — so every separation internal (skimmer, baffles/shroud, coalescer media, sight tube, vents, bulkheads, transfer pump, strainer, float switch, bladder/jerricans) nests inside it and ships as the kit. Only the drum itself and the aerosol flat-black paint are truly source-local; long straight PVC for the S-return is builder-cut to fit the as-built layout.

parts.name: 55-gal reactor/settler drum (the vessel AND the shipping container)
parts.chosenComponent: Eagle 1655MBLKBR — 55-gal open-head HDPE, black blow-molded with UV inhibitors, metal bolt-ring gasketed lid (~23 in dia x ~34 in tall)
parts.vendor: Justrite/Eagle (eagle.justrite.com); Uline S-9945BL as cheaper lever-lock alt
parts.fitsNote: This IS the ~22.5 in x 33 in kit drum — it does not ship inside itself. The Eagle exactly matches the IMPROVED spec (UV-stabilized black HDPE + metal bolt ring, vented not pressure-rated). Uline S-9945BL is fine but lever-lock, not bolt-ring.
parts.upgrade: Eagle bolt-ring over Uline lever-lock — the gasketed metal ring reseals flat and clamps the added baffles/vent penetrations better; worth the ~$80 delta on the one part that holds ~460 lb of slurry.

parts.name: Floating weir surface skimmer head (self-leveling)
parts.chosenComponent: Shop-built HDPE floating-box weir feeding the diaphragm-pump suction (small poly float + adjustable overflow lip) — the honest $30–60 DIY per the manual
parts.vendor: DIY (HDPE offcut + float) shipped precut; SkimOIL FWS as the buy-it option
parts.fitsNote: The film to catch is only ~1/8 in thick, so the intake must self-level at the surface. A small shop-built floating weir nests inside the drum for shipping; a full industrial FWS is overkill and 10x the cost for a 23-in drum.
parts.upgrade: SkimOIL FWS (floating weir skimmer) — one moving part (weir hinge), self-adjusts to any suction pump and to wave action; buy it if the DIY box weir won't hold a calm lip on a pitching raft.

parts.name: Anti-slosh baffle(s) + skimmer stilling shroud
parts.chosenComponent: Precut 1/4-in HDPE baffle plate(s)/slotted center tube + a short open-top poly-bucket shroud around the skim zone
parts.vendor: DIY from HDPE sheet (McMaster 8619K / a poly bucket)
parts.fitsNote: Cut flat and a nesting bucket-shroud both stow inside the drum. Must NOT fully partition the drum (loop still has to circulate) and stays perforated near the bottom for cleanout.
parts.upgrade: none — this is already the cheapest fix for the deepest flaw (gravity separation on a moving boat); a machined slotted center-tube baffle is a marginal refinement, not worth the cost.

parts.name: Coalescer / settler media pack (corrugated-plate)
parts.chosenComponent: Corrugated-plate (cross-flow) coalescing media cut to the 15-gal vessel — PVC/PP plate pack at 1/2–3/4 in spacing
parts.vendor: Wash Bay Solutions / SkimOIL coalescing media; or DIY corrugated PP sheet stack
parts.fitsNote: Stock packs are 1 ft wide x 2 ft high — cut a short section to the ~14.5-in settler and it ships flat inside the drum. Passive, zero power; must be removable for cleaning.
parts.upgrade: Oleophilic coalescing media (e.g., DynaPac-style) over plain corrugated PVC — grabs finer emulsified droplets that cavitation throws; only worth it if commissioning shows the plate pack alone won't break the emulsion.

parts.name: 15-gal intermediate coalescer/settler vessel
parts.chosenComponent: Uline S-24088-class 15-gal open-top HDPE drum (natural/translucent so the oil/water interface is visible), ~14.5 in dia x ~27 in tall
parts.vendor: Uline; Air Sea Containers 15-gal open-head poly as alt
parts.fitsNote: 14.5-in dia x 27-in tall nests inside the 22.5 x 33 drum interior. Pick translucent (not blue) so the sight-line works; paint exterior flat black for passive solar warming.
parts.upgrade: A clear-sided cone-bottom tank over a flat-bottom drum — the cone drains free water cleanly to the S-return and concentrates wax at the top take-off; costs more and won't nest as neatly.

parts.name: Sight glass / level & interface gauge
parts.chosenComponent: NTO 2-in tank sight-gauge kit (2 grommet+barb fittings + clear tube + shutoff), or clear reinforced-vinyl tube + 2 barb-grommets
parts.vendor: NTO Tank (ntotank.com); Ag Spray sight-gauge hose; McMaster sight tubes
parts.fitsNote: Coilable tube + two small fittings; stows loose in the drum. Install top+bottom taps on drum and settler. MUST be UV-shielded (opaque sleeve) — bare clear plastic yellows/embrittles pond-side.
parts.upgrade: Rigid acrylic/borosilicate sight tube with isolation valves over vinyl — reads the interface line more crisply and resists algae fouling; add shutoff valves top and bottom in case the tube fails.

parts.name: Drum penetration fittings (bulkheads)
parts.chosenComponent: UNISEAL flexible tank adapters — 1 in (Amazon B0723HJ9KX) and 2 in (B072QR9KR6); threaded PVC bulkheads where a removable seal is wanted
parts.vendor: Amazon (UNISEAL brand); Banjo/Spears threaded PVC bulkheads at irrigation supply
parts.fitsNote: Small rubber grommets that seal a plain drilled hole — ship loose. Cover nozzle return, feed, S-return valve, skim line, 2x sight-tube taps, and vent. Elevation is the whole game; the sight glass lets the builder set them empirically before drilling.
parts.upgrade: Threaded PVC bulkhead + gasket at the S-return/drain ports over a Uniseal — gives a serviceable, valve-able, re-torqueable seal at the two ports that matter most; Uniseals elsewhere are fine and cheaper.

parts.name: Sub-surface "S"-return tube
parts.chosenComponent: 1-in Sch-40 PVC pipe + 2x 90-deg elbows forming an S/gooseneck, screened inlet below the oil layer
parts.vendor: Home Depot / Lowe's / any irrigation supplier
parts.fitsNote: Elbows + short precut nipples + inlet screen ship in the drum; a long straight run (if the built layout needs >33 in) is builder-cut locally. Inlet MUST sit clearly sub-surface or it siphons off product oil instead of clarified water.
parts.upgrade: Add a ball valve at the bulkhead take-off (doubles as cleanout + lets you throttle draw so you don't pull the interface down and re-entrain oil).
parts.link: search: 1 inch schedule 40 PVC pipe and 90 elbow Home Depot

parts.name: Gooseneck vent + insect/debris screen
parts.chosenComponent: Attwood 90-deg P-trap fuel-tank vent (screened, marine) — one on drum, one on settler
parts.vendor: West Marine / BJ's RV & Marine; Acouto 316-SS gooseneck (Amazon B09JKCHBGQ) as alt
parts.price: $10–18 ea ($8–12/pair for shop-bent PVC + SS screen)
parts.fitsNote: Small; ships loose. The inverted-U with screened downward mouth vents displaced air + algae CO2 while blocking rain/bugs. Mandatory safety part — vessels are lidded and vented, NEVER sealed against pressure.
parts.upgrade: 316 stainless gooseneck (Acouto) over plastic if long UV exposure is expected — won't embrittle; otherwise the Attwood marine vent is the proven cheap default.

parts.name: Final storage — cheap inert default
parts.chosenComponent: 2x Air Sea Containers 25L/6.6-gal HDPE jerricans (Amazon B00PREJQ04) + quick-connect off-load tap
parts.vendor: Amazon (Air Sea Containers); Nalgene 20L HDPE jerrican as alt
parts.fitsNote: HDPE is inert to the waxy lipid product. Two 6.6-gal cans can nest in the drum for shipping (bulky) or be sourced locally. Recommended cheap baseline over the bladder — kills the biggest cost uncertainty in the subsystem.
parts.upgrade: Hydrocarbon-rated TPU collapsible bladder (Fuel Safe / Techno Tanks, 15–25 gal, $350–600) — collapses as it empties (no sloshing air space, flexible deck footprint); only worth it if deck trim/space matters more than $300–500. Do NOT substitute a plain water bladder (swells/leaches).

parts.name: Transfer / off-load diaphragm pump (hydrocarbon-compatible)
parts.chosenComponent: SHURFLO 8000-543-238 — 12V DC diaphragm, 1.8 GPM / 100 PSI, Viton valves + Santoprene diaphragm, self-priming
parts.fitsNote: Exactly the spec: Viton/Santoprene wetted parts survive the waxy lipid, and diaphragm action self-primes and moves semi-solid wax a centrifugal bilge pump would stall on. Small — ships inside. Transfer ONLY; keep strictly off the HP nozzle loop.
parts.upgrade: SHURFLO 4008-class (higher-flow, same Santoprene/Viton family) if off-load time matters; but 1.8 GPM is ample for decant and lower inrush is friendlier to the 45 W budget.

parts.name: Inline suction strainer (protects transfer pump)
parts.chosenComponent: Jabsco Pumpgard 46400-0000 in-line strainer, 3/4-in barb (low profile)
parts.fitsNote: Clear-bowl screened basket on the diaphragm-pump suction traps congealed wax lumps before they jam the check valves (the pump's failure point). Small — ships inside. Distinct from the fine nozzle strainers in Subsystem B.
parts.upgrade: none for the scale — the Jabsco Pumpgard is the marine-standard cheap part; just keep the mesh coarse enough not to starve the thick product flow.

parts.name: Level / float switch (fill-level / decant timing)
parts.chosenComponent: SEAFLO marine bilge float switch, 12V (or Rule-A-Matic 35A)
parts.fitsNote: Small; ships inside. Gates the raise-level-to-decant cycle. In the IMPROVED build it's largely superseded by MPPT load-output timing + the sight glass, but a cheap float switch is still valid low-cost level control. Watch: fouls with wax/algae and sticks.
parts.upgrade: Solid-state / optical level sensor (no moving float to foul with wax) if reliability underway matters; or drop it entirely and gate skimming to calm windows via the sight glass, per the improved edition.

parts.name: Flat-black paint (passive solar warming of the settler)
parts.chosenComponent: Rust-Oleum flat-black spray (plastic-compatible / UV) for the 15-gal settler exterior
parts.fitsNote: Aerosol = hazmat/ORM-D, can't ride in the kit drum. Source locally. Warms wax so it's less viscous and separates faster — zero added power. Keep warming MILD; excess gain can soften/stress HDPE.
parts.upgrade: Adhesive black solar-absorber film or a plastic-adhesion primer + flat-black topcoat if the paint won't key to the HDPE — HDPE is notoriously paint-shy; a plastic-bonding primer prevents peel.
parts.link: search: Rust-Oleum flat black spray paint for plastic Home Depot

systems.kitPhilosophy: Every part in this subsystem is small, short, or coilable, so the entire fluid loop ships packed inside the 55-gal drum — nothing here trips the 33-in rule. The builder sources only two things locally: the drum itself (it IS the shipping container / reactor) and bulk low-pressure PVC suction/return hose and pipe by the foot from any hardware store.

parts.name: Intake coarse basket strainer (FP1)
parts.chosenComponent: Groco ARG-755-P 3/4" bronze raw-water strainer with clear sight bowl + plastic basket
parts.vendor: Marine supply (Wholesale Marine / Fisheries Supply / Go2Marine)
parts.fitsNote: ~6 in tall x 4 in — trivially fits the drum. Clear one-piece sight bowl lets the builder SEE the algae mat blinding it (the top field failure) without disassembly; tool-less basket removal for clean-every-run duty.
parts.upgrade: For a cheaper DIY build, drop to a generic clear-bowl inline sediment strainer (~$20, Amazon) or a pond-pump leaf basket; the Groco is the marine-grade pick but overkill on a freshwater demonstrator. A self-cleaning suction screen (Arkal/Amiad) is the step up if you want zero-maintenance intake.

parts.name: Backflushable fine mesh screen filter + ΔP gauge (FP2)
parts.chosenComponent: Rusco 1" Spin-Down sediment filter, 140-mesh (104 µm) 316 screen, w/ bottom flush ball valve; paired 0-100 psi glycerin gauge(s) across it
parts.vendor: Home Depot / irrigation & well-water supply (Rusco, US Water Systems)
parts.fitsNote: ~11 in tall polymer bowl — fits. This is the geometric anti-clog guarantee: 140-mesh opening (104 µm) is smaller than the smallest 0.012 in orifice bore (~305 µm), so nothing that passes can lodge in the nozzle. Flush valve backflushes under load without teardown.
parts.upgrade: Vu-Flow 200-mesh or an Amiad/Arkal self-cleaning spin-down for finer/auto duty. For real instrumentation, use a purpose-made differential-pressure gauge (e.g., Winters PFQ diff gauge, ~$60) instead of two singles so ΔP reads directly.

parts.name: Cavitation HP feed pump — plunger head + BLDC drive (FP5)
parts.chosenComponent: Cat Pumps 2SF-series direct-drive triplex plunger pump head (e.g., 2SF22ES ~2.2 gpm class) + Brushless.com 48V 750W BLDC motor + BLD-750 controller, belt/direct-coupled and regulated down to ~250-400 psi
parts.fitsNote: Pump head ~8x6x6 in, motor ~4 in dia x 8 in, controller palm-sized — all fit the drum with room. This is the keystone 'brain + hardware' the kit exists to supply: no off-the-shelf 24-48V DC triplex exists, so the kit pre-marries a bulletproof Cat plunger head to a 48V BLDC and controller. Cat 2SF is rated far above 400 psi (you throttle down via the unloader), giving huge seal margin.
parts.upgrade: If the builder accepts lower flow (~0.5-1 gpm), a self-contained 24/48V high-pressure MISTING pump (brushless, 1000 psi, ~$150-250, e.g., Aeromist/mid-pressure fog pump) collapses pump+motor+controller into ONE sealed unit — cheaper, simpler, and even truer to the 'hold pressure, cut flow' physics. Flag: confirm its wetted parts tolerate algae grit.

parts.name: Kinetic Nozzle HOLDER — 316L manifold (FP6)
parts.chosenComponent: 316L stainless manifold drilled/tapped for a triangular cluster of 3-4 orifice inserts (10/24 UNC) with a quick-change coupling — CNC one-off (Xometry/SendCutSend) OR DIY from a 316 stainless pipe plug/cross drilled and tapped
parts.vendor: Xometry / Protolabs / SendCutSend (CNC) or McMaster-Carr (316 plug for DIY)
parts.fitsNote: Palm-sized — ships in the drum if pre-machined. Spec corrected to 316L (the source drawing's '306 S.S.' is a nonexistent grade). Threaded 10/24 sockets accept cheap standard misting-orifice inserts, converting the old $150-600 machined consumable into a reusable body.
parts.upgrade: For the true triangular micro-cluster geometry from the drawings, order the CNC holder; a builder who just wants it working can tap 3-4 holes into a 316 hex plug and skip the shop entirely. Either way keep it 316L and on a quick-disconnect for borescope inspection.

parts.name: Orifice insert — the consumable jet (FP7)
parts.chosenComponent: Stainless-steel high-pressure misting orifice, 0.012 in bore, 10/24 UNC thread (30-pack) — known/defined bore, ~0.029 GPM each @ 1000 psi
parts.fitsNote: Thumbnail-sized; a lifetime of spares fits in a sandwich bag. This is the honest right-sizing of the manual's '$15-40 tungsten-carbide waterblast insert': at 250-400 psi (not 40,000 psi waterjet), a 0.012 in SS misting orifice IS the known-bore jet, at pennies, and fixes orifice area so pump P/Q become predictable.
parts.upgrade: Ceramic or tungsten-carbide misting orifices (10/24) exist for ~10-50x erosion life if the borescope schedule shows real pitting — press-in carbide waterblast inserts (StoneAge/Leland) are the top tier but are over-spec for this pressure. Start SS, upgrade to ceramic/carbide only if erosion data demands it.

parts.name: Unloader / pressure-relief valve (FP9)
parts.chosenComponent: General Pump / AR pressure-washer unloader, low-flow variant (AR ZK7-25 class or General Pump ZK7), bypass routed back to drum; adjustable to hold ~250-400 psi below the 4000-psi hose rating
parts.fitsNote: Fist-sized brass — ships easily. Mandatory life-safety part on a positive-displacement pump: a blocked nozzle has nowhere to send flow and will burst the line without it. Its bypass return doubles as in-drum mixing (which is why the separate immersion pump got deleted).
parts.upgrade: Flag: at 1.5-2.5 gpm you are BELOW most bypass-unloaders' actuation flow (ZK7.1 min ~2.9 gpm). Prefer a simple spring-loaded adjustable PRESSURE-REGULATING/RELIEF valve sized for low flow over a flow-actuated unloader — it regulates cleanly at trickle flow where a bypass unloader chatters.

parts.name: High-pressure hose + fittings (FP10)
parts.chosenComponent: 3/8 in (or 1/4 in) pressure-washer hose, 4000 psi, wire-braided, M22/QC ends for the NOZZLE-FEED LEG ONLY (e.g., Corretic/RIDGE WASHER) + low-pressure reinforced PVC hose, ball valves, tees, barbs, check valves for the rest
parts.fitsNote: Coils flat — HP hose and the fittings kit ship in the drum. Only the single nozzle-feed leg is HP-rated; everything else is ordinary reinforced PVC. 1/4 in ID is plenty at 1.5-2.5 gpm and keeps the coil small.
parts.upgrade: Bulk low-pressure PVC hose and Sch-40 pipe are cheapest bought locally by the foot (source-locally). Use proper HP threaded/QC ends on the feed leg — barbed clamps creep and weep at 400 psi.

parts.name: Intake / transfer bilge lift pump (FP3)
parts.chosenComponent: Rule-Mate or Attwood Tsunami T500 12V bilge cartridge, ~500-800 GPH, 3/4 in outlet
parts.fitsNote: Palm-sized cartridge — ships. Low-pressure volume lift only (pond -> drum through the coarse strainer); a few psi, so it CANNOT and MUST NOT feed the nozzle. Size GPH to drum turnover, not the box number (nameplate collapses against real lift head).
parts.upgrade: A 12V self-priming diaphragm pump avoids the centrifugal air-lock problem if the pump sits above the waterline. Otherwise this $30 throwaway is the right 'borrow a marine part' call.

parts.name: Off-load / decant diaphragm pump (FP12)
parts.chosenComponent: Pentair SHURFLO 8000-543-250 12VDC diaphragm pump — 1.8 GPM, 50 PSI, Viton valves + Santoprene diaphragm (hydrocarbon-compatible wetted parts)
parts.fitsNote: Small — ships. Transfer duty ONLY (skimmed wax/oil -> jerricans/bladder). Self-priming diaphragm moves viscous/semi-solid wax a centrifugal pump can't. Viton/Santoprene wetted parts survive the waxy lipid product where plain Buna swells. Keep it STRICTLY off the HP loop — plumbing it to the nozzle destroys it.
parts.upgrade: SHURFLO SF-1100 bulk chemical transfer (higher flow) if off-load speed matters; add an inline suction strainer either way to keep wax lumps out of the check valves.

parts.name: Eductor / venturi injector (FP8) — DAF concentration + mixing
parts.chosenComponent: Mazzei 584 (1/2 in) or 878 (1 in) polypropylene venturi injector — no-moving-parts, entrains gas to float/concentrate algae toward the >6% solids target
parts.fitsNote: Palm-sized polymer part — ships. Fed from the unloader bypass so it keeps floating/mixing while the HP pump idles between batches. Sizing to slurry flow is UNKNOWN — match motive flow (584 = 5.9 gpm @ 40 psi; 878 = 10.3 gpm) to your recirc leg, or measure.
parts.upgrade: Size the model to your actual recirc flow after the pump is chosen; too-small motive flow gives too little suction to float anything. The custom 4-port part in the drawings is unnecessary — a COTS Mazzei is the honest stand-in.

parts.name: Inline instrumentation — flow/pressure/watt (FP11)
parts.chosenComponent: Glycerin-filled 0-600 psi HP gauge + hall-effect/paddlewheel flow sensor (~1.5-2.5 gpm range) + inline DC watt-meter (shunt, e.g., Bayite/Drok) on the pump circuit
parts.vendor: Amazon (gauges, DC meters) + process-instrument supply (GPI, Blue-White for the flow meter)
parts.fitsNote: All small — ships. This ~$100 of gauges is the cheapest-but-highest-stakes part in the build: it turns every run into logged grams-oil-out vs. watt-hours-in and reads TRUE nozzle P/Q off the gauge (never the BOM caption). Glycerin fill is mandatory — a dry gauge needle hammers itself dead on plunger-pump pulsation.
parts.upgrade: For real logging, feed the DC shunt and a pressure transducer into the optional ESP32 so runs auto-log; the Victron SmartShunt already covers battery-side Wh but a dedicated pump-circuit watt-meter isolates the cavitation energy cost.
